description: Chart 14 — Does proximity to transport help venues survive? Two-year survival of the July 2023 liquor-licence cohort (still licensed in July 2025), by walking distance to the nearest stop, split metro (teal) / regional (orange). The lines are flat-to-rising: being NEAR a stop does not raise survival, and in metro the closest band actually churns slightly more. Lines/points (not bars) so the y-axis can zoom to the 80–95% range where the small differences live without a misleading truncated-bar baseline. Survival is a proxy: a ceased licence can be a sale/relocation/rename, not only a closure — association, never causation. Data: chart_survival_distance_band.csv (8 rows).

title.text: Being near transport doesn't keep venues open
title.subtitle: Two-year survival of 2023 venues by distance to the nearest stop. Every band survives 87–93%; if anything, metro venues nearest a stop close slightly more.
